x402Payment.description: x402 v2 USDC payment. First call without this header returns 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header (base64 JSON quote) and a JSON body with the same `accepts` block. Sign the quoted transfer and retry the **identical** request with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. Legacy header `x-payment` is also accepted. Required when `payment.status` is "live" (see /.well-known/service.json). Flow: https://readfetch.com/SKILL.md and https://readfetch.com/docs.
x402Payment.name: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE

info.description: Pay-per-call web reading for AI agents over x402 — no account, no API key. Reading routes settle on delivery; /v1/fetch when the origin answers. Signed provenance on paid responses. Start free with POST /v1/probe. Paid routes require x402 (see components.securitySchemes). Check `payment.status` in /.well-known/service.json before choosing PAYMENT-SIGNATURE vs stub `x-payment-proof`. `info.version` is API semver only; `x-readfetch-deployment-version` matches service.json `version` (includes the site build counter when present).
info.title: readfetch.com

post.description: Read a fixed list of public HTML pages in one call—the same article extraction as POST /v1/text for each URL (Markdown or plain text plus title and metadata). One x402 payment covers the batch (minimum 10 pages quoted; URLs deduped, max 50). Returns results in input order: each item has url, status_code, text, billed, and hint when undelivered, plus batch-level delivered, failed, billed_pages, and optional credit for unused pages. Undelivered pages are not billed. Use readfetch_text for one URL, readfetch_map then readfetch_crawl to discover and walk a site, readfetch_scrape when JavaScript is required. Read-only; 402 without PAYMENT-SIGNATURE like other paid tools.

post.description: Start a bounded async crawl from one seed URL. Returns job_id, status (queued), pages_quoted, and price_usd — then poll readfetch_crawl_status with that id until status is complete or failed. A complete job includes per-page url and Markdown in the status payload. Cap scope with max_pages (default 20, max 100) and max_depth (default 2, max 3); include/exclude filter paths by prefix (* suffix on include). Prefer readfetch_batch for a fixed URL list; readfetch_map to list URLs without fetching bodies; readfetch_text for a single page.

Results are kept for one hour after the job finishes.

post.description: Stateless change detection on readable page text (same HTTP-first extraction as readfetch_text): fetch the URL, compare to a hash or prior body you store client-side, return changed/unchanged plus optional line diff. First call with no prior fields returns a baseline hash (see hint). `previous_hash` alone detects change without a line diff; add `previous_content` when you need added/removed/diff. A no-change answer is still billable when text was delivered. Prefer readfetch_text when you need the full article once; readfetch_probe (free) for a short preview and `content_sha256` before spending on text.

previous_hash.description: `sha256:…` or bare hex from readfetch_diff, readfetch_probe `content_sha256`, or a prior text read. Omit on the first poll to establish a baseline hash in the response.

timeout_s.description: Total budget for the whole call in seconds, both fetches included. 60 s is the ceiling on this route.

Use `json_body` for JSON POST/PUT payloads; use `body` for raw bytes or strings. Prefer readfetch_text for readable HTML articles; readfetch_pdf to extract PDF text (not raw bytes alone). POST/PUT/DELETE can change remote state despite readOnlyHint.

post.description: Extract text from a PDF (%PDF- magic, not Content-Type). Send exactly one of `url` (public http(s) link — egress GET, ≤ 20 MB) or `content_base64` (bytes you already have — the whole request body is capped at 1 MiB, base64 expansion included; optional `filename` labels the upload). Returns `pages` (per-page text), one concatenated `markdown` body, `title`, and `metadata`; $0.005 per document, not per page. `max_pages` limits extraction (default 50, max 200); documents over 200 pages or above your cap return 413 and are not billed. Scanned/image-only PDFs may return empty text with `billed: false` and a `hint`. Prefer readfetch_text or readfetch_scrape for HTML articles; readfetch_fetch for raw PDF bytes without extraction; readfetch_batch for many HTML URLs, not PDFs. Read-only server-side; paid x402 like other routes.

content_base64.description: Base64-encoded PDF bytes. The request body is capped at 1 MiB total — base64 expansion comes out of that, it does not add to it (~0.75 MB of PDF). Mutually exclusive with url; pair with filename when the label matters.

filename.description: Optional label when using content_base64 (default upload.pdf); ignored for url-only requests.

max_pages.description: Extract at most this many pages. Default 50; raise up to 200 when the document is longer. Over cap → 413, unbilled.

url.description: Public PDF URL; fetched through egress (≤ 20 MB). Mutually exclusive with content_base64.

post.description: Free preflight on a URL before any paid readfetch_* call: HTTP status, content type, byte size, title, language, and whether a bot wall is waiting (`challenge`). When the response is HTML and not a challenge page, the JSON includes **`preview`**: up to **400 characters** of the text readfetch_text would return (same extractor). Use readfetch_probe instead of readfetch_text when choosing a route or estimating size; if `challenge: true`, use readfetch_scrape (then readfetch_residential if still blocked), not readfetch_text. post.description: Screenshot a public URL in headless Chromium (page JavaScript runs; no ad blocker) and return PNG or JPEG in JSON — `image_base64`, `mime`, `width`, `height`, `status_code`, `billed` (not a hosted URL). Scope: viewport only (`full_page: false`), full scrollable page (default), or one element (`selector`). `mode` caps total render time: fast (15 s), render (30 s, default), full (60 s, always full-page regardless of `full_page`). Set `width`/`height` before navigation (default 1280×800, max 3840×2160). `delay_ms` (0–30000) waits after navigation, then captures — raise it or use `mode=full` for slow SPAs and lazy media. Prefer readfetch_text or readfetch_scrape for extractable text; readfetch_pdf for PDF files; readfetch_fetch for raw HTTP without rendering. Read-only on the origin (GET + render, no form POST). Bot-check or blank frames may still return pixels with `billed: false` and a `hint`; paid x402 like other routes.
